forward_guidance.text: The 10-Q contains no quantitative revenue, margin or EPS guidance for the next quarter or the full year. The filing gives only qualitative forward-looking statements: Helios rack-scale platforms are expected to start shipping in the second half of fiscal 2026; OpenAI and Meta each intend to deploy up to 6 gigawatts of AMD data center GPUs, with the first gigawatt of each powered by Instinct MI450 series; $17.4B of unconditional commitments fall in the remainder of 2026; long-term data center leases of $9.5B are expected to commence in 2027 and 2028; investment commitments of up to $5.0B are expected to be made through fiscal 2028; and 2026 remaining intangible amortization is estimated at $1,062M. Management also expects cash, short-term investments, operating cash flow, the revolver and commercial paper to be sufficient for the next 12 months and beyond.
forward_guidance.source_citation: 10-Q Part I, Item 2 MD&A (Overview and Recent Developments; Liquidity and Capital Resources); Note 6; Note 8; Note 10; Part II, Item 1A Risk Factors (Helios timing)

key_risks.description: Customer concentration: a small number of customers account for a substantial portion of revenue and receivables, and loss of a significant customer would materially affect results. Large AI deployments (OpenAI, Meta at up to 6 GW each) deepen dependence on a few customers.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part II, Item 1A, Economic and Strategic Risks - loss of a significant customer; Item 2 MD&A Overview

key_risks.description: Warrant dilution and vesting: OpenAI and Meta warrants for up to 160M shares each at $0.01 exercise price, vesting on GPU purchase milestones and stock price targets. None had vested at June 27, 2026. Classified as liabilities until conditions for equity classification are met.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part I, Item 1, Note 12 Common Stock and Stock-based Compensation - Warrants (Meta warrant issued February 2026)

key_risks.description: Export controls and China exposure: MI308 and MI325 sales to China depend on licenses, China import rules and customer demand. MI325 shipments must be inspected in the US and are subject to a 25% tariff on importation. The US government has expressed an expectation of 15% of licensed MI308 China revenue, but no regulation has been published. New Chinese regulations (Decrees 834 and 835) could create conflicting legal obligations.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part II, Item 1A, Legal and Regulatory Risks - Government actions and regulations, including export controls

key_risks.description: Large and growing supply and lease obligations: $30.3B of unconditional commitments (including cloud compute capacity), $4.5B of uncommenced leases, a further $9.5B of data center leases signed after quarter end, $4.1B of data center lease guarantees for commercial partners, and up to $5.0B of new investment commitments. Demand shortfalls could leave excess inventory or capacity.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part I, Item 1, Note 8 Financial Instruments (Lease Guarantees); Note 10 Commitments and Contingencies; Item 2 MD&A Liquidity

key_risks.description: Industry-wide memory shortage and rising memory prices could constrain supply, raise production costs and pressure gross margin, and could raise data center build-out costs for customers.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part II, Item 1A, Economic and market uncertainty; Essential equipment, materials, substrates risk factors

key_risks.description: Dependence on third-party manufacturing: TSMC makes all wafers at 7nm or smaller nodes, GF supplies larger nodes, and the ATMP JVs provide most assembly and test. Supply constraints, yield problems or prioritization of other customers could limit shipments.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part II, Item 1A, Operational and Technology Risks - We rely on third parties to manufacture our products

key_risks.description: Rack-scale (Helios) execution risk: Helios is expected to start shipping in 2H FY2026, relies on numerous third-party rack-level components, and AMD does not manufacture or sell completed Helios rack systems. Product transitions complicate supply and demand management.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part II, Item 1A, Success of business depends on ability to introduce products on a timely basis; Essential equipment, materials risk factors

key_risks.description: Competition: Nvidia's data center GPU position and software ecosystem, Intel's aggressive pricing, Arm-based architectures and customer in-house AI silicon. The Nvidia-Intel partnership announced in September 2025 may add pricing pressure.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part II, Item 1A, Economic and Strategic Risks - markets are highly competitive

key_risks.description: AI demand and customer financing risk: AI customers may lack data center capacity, power or capital and may seek alternative financing or deferred-payment arrangements, delaying or reducing demand. The long-term trajectory of AI demand is described as uncertain.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part II, Item 1A, The demand for our products depends in part on the market conditions in the industries into which they are sold

key_risks.description: Earnings quality and investment volatility: Q2 other income included large unrealized gains on newly public equity securities, subject to market risk and sale restrictions through October 2028. Marketable equity securities were 1.2B and non-marketable 1.7B at quarter end.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part I, Item 3 Market Risk - Long-term Investment Risk; Note 8 Financial Instruments

key_risks.description: Semi-custom and Gaming dependence on console partners' product success; Gaming revenue fell 31% in Q2.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part II, Item 1A, Semi-custom SoC risk factor; Item 2 MD&A, Client and Gaming

key_risks.description: ZT Systems divestiture exposure: post-closing working capital adjustments (243M paid in Q2), and a 348M earn-out receivable (up to 450M possible) subject to impairment assessment.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part I, Item 1, Note 5 Acquisitions and Divestitures

bull_case: Q2 revenue grew 50% YoY to $11.5B, with Data Center revenue up 107% to $6.7B on EPYC and Instinct MI350 demand, and Data Center operating income of $2.1B.
Gross margin recovered to 54% from 40% (prior year included MI308 export-control charges), and operating income reached $2.0B versus a loss a year ago.
Large multi-year AI commitments from OpenAI and Meta (up to 6 GW each, starting with MI450) and Helios rack-scale shipments expected in 2H FY2026 provide a visible product and demand pipeline.
Client revenue grew 23% on a 34% rise in unit shipments, and Embedded grew 19% as demand strengthened across end markets.
Strong liquidity: $13.1B of cash and short-term investments against $3.25B of debt, $5.3B of six-month operating cash flow, a new $5.0B revolver and a $5.5B commercial paper program, all undrawn.
Warrants issued to OpenAI and Meta have not vested, so there has been no dilution or financial statement impact to date.
bear_case: Q2 pre-tax income was lifted by $598M of other income, mostly unrealized gains on newly listed investments. These are non-operating, may reverse, and are partly subject to sale restrictions.
Opex is growing fast (R&D +33%, MG&A +41%, SBC +36%), and Client and Gaming operating income fell to $582M from $767M.
Gaming revenue fell 31% on weaker semi-custom sales, and Client ASP fell 6%, so Client growth relied on unit volume and mix.

Obligations are growing rapidly: $30.3B of unconditional commitments ($17.4B in the remainder of 2026), $9.5B of new data center leases, up to $5.0B of investment commitments and $4.1B of lease guarantees. A demand shortfall could create excess inventory or capacity.

Receivables rose by about $1.0B in six months and inventory by about $0.5B; $1.0B of prepaid assets, mainly supply prepayments, increased; payables rose $2.2B on timing, flattering operating cash flow.
China export licensing, the 25% tariff on MI325 inspection, a possible 15% revenue-share request and Chinese countermeasures create regulatory uncertainty.
Customer concentration and potential warrant dilution (up to 320M shares combined) tied to the largest AI customers; competition from Nvidia, Intel, Arm and customer in-house silicon.
Memory shortage and rising memory prices could pressure gross margin and customers' data center build costs.

what_to_watch.text: Q3 FY2026 results (quarter ended September 26, 2026): whether Data Center revenue and the ~54% gross margin hold sequentially. The 10-Q provides no formal guidance, so compare against management's earnings-call outlook and consensus.
Helios rack-scale and Instinct MI450 launch timing and initial shipments in 2H FY2026, and any first progress toward OpenAI/Meta warrant vesting milestones.
China exposure: MI308 shipments, whether MI325 imports are permitted into China, the 25% inspection tariff, and any US revenue-share regulation.
Operating expense trajectory (R&D, MG&A, SBC) versus revenue growth, and operating margin excluding investment gains.

Working capital and commitments: inventory, receivables, supply prepayments, the $17.4B of 2026 commitments, and the $9.5B of new data center leases and up to $5.0B of investment commitments entered into after quarter end.
Gaming and semi-custom trend, and Client unit versus ASP dynamics in the second half.
Other income and investment mark-to-market changes, and the effective tax rate (9.8% in Q2).
Treasury actions: repayment or refinancing of the $875M 4.212% notes due September 2026, and the pace of share repurchases ($9.2B remaining; only $221M repurchased in six months).
Memory supply and pricing effects on gross margin and customer build-outs.

data_gaps: No quantitative forward guidance (next-quarter revenue, gross margin, opex, tax rate) is in the 10-Q; the earnings press release or 8-K was not provided.
No recent news items were provided or sourced, so recent_news is empty; no URLs were fabricated.
No analyst consensus estimates or stock price data were provided, so there is no expectations comparison.
Non-GAAP measures (non-GAAP gross margin, operating income, EPS, free cash flow) are not in the 10-Q; only GAAP figures are cited. The operating cash flow less capex figure is analyst-derived.
The 10-Q does not disclose customer concentration percentages or the Data Center split between Instinct GPU and EPYC CPU revenue, so AI accelerator revenue cannot be quantified.
The 10-Q does not quantify MI308 or MI325 China revenue in Q2, nor gross margin by segment.

Q1 FY2026 standalone figures and the prior-year 10-K were not provided, so sequential comparisons are not made and 'is_new' flags on risks reflect dating within the 10-Q (2026-dated events), not a comparison with prior filings.
Q3 FY2026 results (quarter ended September 26, 2026) were not provided; this report is based on data through June 27, 2026 and may be stale at the report date.
Details of the up to $5.0B post-quarter investment commitments and the counterparties of the $9.5B data center leases are not disclosed.

hypotheses_explored.question: Is the margin recovery driven by structural mix shift toward Data Center rather than just the absence of prior-year charges?
hypotheses_explored.summary: Gross margin rose to 54% from 40%, but the filing attributes the improvement both to the absence of MI308 charges and to favorable mix including higher Data Center revenue. Data Center operating income reached $2.1B on $6.7B revenue (about 31% segment margin), supporting a mix component, though the prior-year base was depressed by about $440M of annual net charges. Sustainability depends on MI450/Helios ramp costs and memory prices.
evidence_quotes: Gross margin for the three months ended June 27, 2026 was 54% compared to gross margin of 40% for the prior year period

The increase in both periods was driven by the absence of inventory and related charges associated with the U.S. government export control on AMD Instinct MI308 Data Center GPU products that was recorded in the prior year period and a favorable product mix, including higher Data Center segment revenue.

hypotheses_explored.question: How much of Q2 net income quality depends on non-operating investment gains?
hypotheses_explored.summary: Other income of $598M, primarily unrealized gains on newly listed equity securities, represents about 23% of Q2 pre-tax income of $2,551M. Operating income of $1,990M is the cleaner indicator. A low effective tax rate of 9.8% also supports EPS. Investment gains are subject to market volatility and sale restrictions through October 2028.
evidence_quotes: The increase in both periods was primarily driven by unrealized gains from the public market listing of non-marketable equity securities during the second quarter of fiscal year 2026.

hypotheses_explored.question: Do rising commitments and lease obligations create meaningful downside if AI demand slows?
hypotheses_explored.summary: Unconditional commitments of $30.3B (with $17.4B due in 2026), uncommenced leases of $4.5B, $9.5B of new post-quarter leases, $4.1B of lease guarantees and up to $5.0B of investment commitments significantly exceed $13.1B of cash and short-term investments. Strong operating cash flow and undrawn $5.0B revolver plus $5.5B commercial paper capacity mitigate near-term liquidity risk, but a demand shortfall could create excess inventory or capacity.
evidence_quotes: As of June 27, 2026, we had unconditional commitments of approximately $30.3 billion, of which $17.4 billion are for the remainder of fiscal year 2026.
